sentence_stem: Not only did the team win the championship,
correct_completion: but they also broke the national record.
full_sentence: Not only did the team win the championship, but they also broke the national record.
acceptable_variants: but they also set a new national record.
but they also achieved a record for the nation.

options.text: did they celebrate with the fans.
options.why_wrong: This is a yes/no question form and does not complete the 'not only ... but also' structure.

options.text: they celebrated with the fans in the stadium.
options.why_wrong: This is a separate statement that ignores the second element of 'not only ... but also', so the correlative structure is left incomplete.

options.text: so they broke the national record.
options.why_wrong: 'So' signals a result, but 'not only ... but also' requires an additional element, not a consequence.

options.text: but they also broke the national record.

grammar_focus: Inversion after the negative adverbial 'Not only' with the correlative 'but also'
explanation: 'Not only' at the start of a sentence triggers subject-auxiliary inversion in the first clause, and the second clause must begin with 'but also' to complete the pair. Spanish speakers often expect a single clause without inversion, so they may omit the second element or use a result connector instead.
translation: No solo el equipo ganó el campeonato, sino que también batió el récord nacional.
